overview: Woolworths Group is Australia and New Zealand's largest food retailer, operating supermarkets under the Woolworths, Countdown/Woolworths NZ, and BIG W (general merchandise) banners, alongside the B2B food distributor PFD Food Services and pet retailer Petstock. Since demerging its Endeavour Group liquor/hospitality business (ALH Hotels, Dan Murphy's, BWS) effective 30 June 2021, Woolworths has operated as a focused food and everyday-needs retailer, supplemented by complementary businesses and services including Everyday Rewards loyalty, Cartology retail media, and Primary Connect logistics. The Group serves roughly 26 million customer transactions a week across a network of 1,729 retail stores.

business_model.summary: Woolworths is a scale grocery and general-merchandise retailer that earns thin net retail margins on high transaction volumes, supplemented by higher-margin complementary businesses (loyalty/media/B2B logistics) that leverage its retail data and customer base. Revenue is overwhelmingly transactional/recurring in nature (weekly grocery spend is non-discretionary and sticky), with growth increasingly monetized through digital/eCommerce, retail media (Cartology), and Everyday Rewards (13M+ members).

revenue_streams.name: New Zealand Food
revenue_streams.trend: stable/mixed (strong in NZD, weak in AUD)

revenue_streams.name: W Living (BIG W + other general merchandise)
Complementary services (Everyday Rewards, Cartology, Primary Connect)
revenue_streams.percent: not separately disclosed as % of Group revenue; material EBIT contributor (~1/3 of FY26 EBIT growth)

business_model.customer_type: Primarily B2C mass-market grocery and general merchandise consumers across Australia and New Zealand; PFD serves B2B customers (QSR chains, foodservice, hospitality)
business_model.geographic_mix: Predominantly Australia (Australian Food ~75% of Group sales), with New Zealand Food (Countdown/Woolworths NZ) contributing roughly 10%; minimal exposure outside ANZ

competitive_position.market_position: Market leader in Australian grocery with an estimated 36-38% share of food and grocery retailing, ahead of Coles (~28-29%); Woolworths and Coles together hold roughly 65-67% of the market, making Australian grocery a tight duopoly (plus Aldi as the significant discount-format challenger at ~9-12% and growing)

moat_factors.description: 86% of the Australian population lives within a 10-minute drive of a Woolworths supermarket; scale underpins buying power and logistics efficiency (Primary Connect, new Moorebank automated distribution centre completed FY2026)

Everyday Rewards has 13M+ members; proprietary data and AI (e.g., Olive digital shopping assistant, Quantium analytics JV) support personalization, Cartology retail media monetization, and supplier insights
100-year-old brand heritage and largest store network in ANZ, but brand strength has been dented by pricing scrutiny and the payroll scandal
eCommerce sales penetration ~15.9% of Group sales (up ~5pts over 3 years); 90% of Australian population covered by the eCommerce network; On Demand/Direct to Boot convenience formats scaling fast

High barriers to entry in large-format grocery (site access, supply chain, planning approvals) have historically protected Woolworths/Coles share, though this is also the source of intense regulatory scrutiny

weaknesses: Thin net margins typical of grocery retail leave limited room for cost shocks or price wars
New Zealand Food has underperformed with a large FY2024 goodwill impairment and continued soft trading/market growth
BIG W/general merchandise has been structurally challenged, only returning to profit in FY2026 after a prior-year loss
Reputational damage from wage underpayment scandal and pricing/discount-claims litigation
Vulnerable to further share gains by Aldi (lower-cost operating model) and emerging low-cost/online entrants (Costco expansion, potential Amazon Fresh moves)

growth_drivers: eCommerce and 'ultra-convenience' growth: Group eCommerce sales +15.9% in FY2026 to $10.6B; On Demand delivery more than doubled in two years; Direct to Boot now in 785 stores
Retail media and data monetization via Cartology, leveraging Quantium analytics and the Everyday Rewards member base
Supply chain modernization: completion of the Moorebank Regional Distribution Centre (opened November 2025) expected to unlock efficiency and productivity savings
AI/agentic technology: five-year strategic partnership with Google Cloud; Olive digital shopping assistant; Gemini Enterprise rollout; automation of ~60% of customer service contacts

Turnaround of underperforming segments: BIG W returned to profit in FY2026; New Zealand Food targeting a return to double-digit returns over the medium term via a new store operating model and relaunched Member Prices
Complementary businesses (Petstock, PFD B2B foodservice, Rewards & Services) contributed roughly a third of FY2026 EBIT growth and represent a diversification/growth lever beyond core supermarkets
Above-store cost savings program (~$400M delivered in FY2026) supporting margin recovery and reinvestment in price/value

business.description: Aldi continues to take share with a lower-cost model; Coles rivalry has intensified; Costco and potential further Amazon grocery expansion add pressure, especially given weak consumer sentiment and cost-of-living pressure (62% of customers rate cost-of-living as their top issue per FY2026 annual report)

FY2024 ~A$1,492M goodwill impairment on NZ Food reflected structurally weaker returns; FY2026 saw a second-half earnings dip from disruption related to a new store operating model rollout, despite local-currency sales growth
Only recently returned to profitability after a loss; sustaining the turnaround (range, clothing, BIG W Market expansion) is unproven over a full cycle
Payroll underpayment scandal and ACCC discount-claims litigation have damaged customer and brand trust, requiring sustained investment to rebuild (per CEO/Chair commentary in FY2026 annual report)

financial.description: Lease accounting (effective FY2020) materially increased recognized lease liabilities and right-of-use assets; large store/property footprint means ongoing lease renewal and rent-escalation exposure
New Zealand Food sales/earnings reported in AUD are volatile to currency moves — FY2026 NZ Food sales were +2.5% in NZD but -3.1% in AUD

H1 FY2026 booked a ~A$710M payroll remediation provision plus ~A$20M associated interest; further provisions/interest, superannuation and payroll tax adjustments are possible as the class action and remediation process continues

regulatory.description: ACCC sued Woolworths (and Coles) in September 2024 over allegedly misleading 'Prices Dropped'/'Down Down' discount claims; the ACCC's broader 2024-2025 supermarket pricing inquiry increased political and regulatory attention on margins and supplier relationships; a mandatory Food and Grocery Code with penalties for excessive pricing by large retailers took effect 1 July 2026

Federal Court proceedings over salaried store team leader underpayments resulted in a major remediation program; Woolworths estimated further post-tax remediation costs in the hundreds of millions (A$180-330M range flagged by the company in 2025, since partly reflected in the H1 FY2026 A$710M provision); litigation and potential appeals remain ongoing

Repeated Senate and government inquiries into supermarket pricing and the Coles/Woolworths duopoly keep political risk elevated, including potential for further code-of-conduct tightening, divestiture debate, or additional compliance costs

macro.risk: Cost-of-living pressure on discretionary and even grocery spend mix
macro.description: Persistent inflation and historically elevated interest rates have entrenched value-seeking behavior; management flagged 'record low consumer confidence and rising costs' as a backdrop in FY2026

Wage increases (4.0% FY2026 award increase for Australian store teams), freight/fuel costs, and supply chain costs linked to geopolitical volatility (e.g., Middle East conflict impact on fuel pricing) pressure margins
Global conflict and geopolitical volatility can disrupt supply availability; Group has responded by raising inventory days (31.3 days in FY2026, up 1.1 days) to build buffer stock

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Australian/NZ grocery retail is a large, mature, low-growth-but-defensive industry (population growth plus modest inflation-driven nominal growth); supermarkets are largely non-discretionary, making the sector relatively resilient through economic cycles, though trading down to private label and discount formats increases during cost-of-living stress
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low-to-moderate — grocery is defensive/non-discretionary, but general merchandise (BIG W) and discretionary categories are more cyclical and sensitive to consumer sentiment
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate indirect sensitivity via consumer discretionary spending and household budgets (cost-of-living pressure cited as a top customer concern); direct balance sheet sensitivity via lease liabilities and any floating-rate debt
key_input_costs: Fresh food/commodity input costs (grocery, meat, produce)

recent_developments.event: FY2026 full-year results (52 weeks to 28 June 2026): Group sales +3.6% to A$71.5B; Group EBIT before significant items +12.7% to A$3,105M; NPAT before significant items +15.4% to A$1,599M; statutory NPAT +18.1% to A$1,138M (impacted by the A$710M payroll remediation charge booked as a significant item); full-year dividend +15.5% to 97cps fully franked. Australian Food EBIT +8.5%; BIG W returned to profit; eCommerce sales +15.9%.

H1 FY2026 results: Group sales +3.4% to A$37.1B, underlying EBIT +14.4% to A$1.66B, but statutory NPAT fell sharply (reported ~49% decline in one account) due to the ~A$710M end-to-end payroll review remediation provision plus ~A$20M interest accrual recognized as a significant item.
Moorebank Regional Distribution Centre (NSW) opened, completing a multi-year automated ambient grocery supply chain renewal expected to deliver efficiency/productivity gains.

Terry Bowen appointed as a new non-executive director, bringing capital allocation, transformation and supply chain expertise; Jon Alferness (ex-Walmart US Chief Product Officer) joined the Board in March 2026, adding digital/technology expertise; Tracey Fellows retired from the Board in March 2026.
Announced a new five-year strategic technology partnership with Google Cloud and continued rollout of agentic AI (Olive shopping assistant, Gemini Enterprise) across the business.

Woolworths and Coles continue to face ACCC litigation over allegedly misleading 'Down Down'/'Prices Dropped' discount claims (filed September 2024); a new Food and Grocery Code of Conduct with penalties for excessive pricing by large retailers took effect 1 July 2026; political/parliamentary scrutiny of supermarket pricing and the duopoly has remained persistent through 2025-2026.

Wage underpayment class action (salaried store team leaders) remains in litigation; company flagged potential further remediation costs (post-tax estimate in the A$180-330M range flagged in 2025) beyond amounts already provisioned; case management and potential appeal processes continuing into 2026.

Q1 FY2027 trading update: Group sales +4.7% to ~A$19.35B; Australian Food sales growth accelerating (+6.9%, with CEO commentary citing Australian Food total sales momentum continuing into FY2027 after +4.6% FY2026 growth, +5.7% in H2); New Zealand Food soft in AUD terms; BIG W slightly negative.

Broker reaction to FY2026 results mixed-to-positive: Bell Potter raised price target to A$42.35 (from A$35.50); Morgans maintained an 'accumulate' rating with target raised to A$43.50; overall sell-side consensus remained closer to 'Hold' with average targets in the mid-A$30s to low-A$40s range and a wide spread of views, including at least one reported sell rating (UBS) despite a raised target.

guidance.as_of: FY2026 Full-Year Results (26 August 2026) and Q1 FY2027 trading update

items.target: Momentum continuing into FY2027; Q1 FY2027 Australian Food sales +6.9%
items.notes: Management highlighted that sales momentum built through H2 FY2026 (5.7% growth) continued into the start of FY2027

items.target: Woolworths Food Retail sales growth in line with or above market; Woolworths Food Retail EBIT growth greater than sales growth; incremental growth from complementary businesses and services; double-digit Total Shareholder Return (TSR)
items.notes: These are the Group's standing medium-term financial aspirations restated in the FY2026 Annual Report, not single-year point guidance

items.target: ~$400 million delivered in FY2026, in line with expectations; continued focus on productivity/cost discipline into FY2027
items.notes: No explicit new-year dollar target disclosed in the material reviewed; framed as an ongoing low-cost retailing priority

items.metric: New Zealand Food and BIG W returns
items.target: Priority to restore sales momentum and deliver improved financial performance; medium-term ambition for double-digit returns
items.vs_prior: maintained but trading conditions flagged as remaining subdued in NZ
items.notes: Management explicitly cautioned that NZ Food trading conditions are expected to remain subdued near-term despite improving customer metrics

guidance.management_commentary: Chair Scott Perkins and CEO Amanda Bardwell both emphasized FY2026 as a year of 'rebuilding momentum' following a weaker FY2025, with improved performance across all segments, but cautioned that the Group's momentum 'offers no assurance that it will be sustained' in a 'challenging and intensive competitive market.' Bardwell flagged a 'challenging economic environment and a dynamic competitive landscape' while expressing confidence in continued delivery for customers, team and shareholders in FY2027.

bull_case: Clear earnings turnaround underway: FY2026 delivered double-digit EBIT and NPAT growth across all segments, with BIG W returning to profit and Australian Food EBIT +8.5%, suggesting operational execution and cost discipline are improving after a weak FY2025

Market-leading scale and defensive demand profile: ~36-38% share of a non-discretionary grocery market, dense store network (86% of Australians within 10 minutes), and a large loyalty base (13M+ Everyday Rewards members) support pricing power and resilient cash generation through economic cycles

Multiple growth levers beyond the core supermarket: eCommerce (+15.9% in FY2026), retail media (Cartology), B2B foodservice (PFD), and Petstock together contributed roughly a third of FY2026 EBIT growth, diversifying earnings beyond pure grocery retail

Investment phase largely behind it: completion of the Moorebank automated distribution centre and prior digital/AI infrastructure investment should start converting into visible productivity and margin benefits

Dividend growth and capital discipline: full-year dividend +15.5% to 97cps fully franked in FY2026, signaling confidence in the earnings recovery and providing an attractive income profile for income-focused investors
bear_case: Thin-margin, highly competitive duopoly under siege: intensifying competition from Aldi, Coles, Costco and potential further e-commerce/discount entrants could compress margins just as the Group is trying to rebuild momentum

Unresolved regulatory and legal overhang: ongoing ACCC litigation over discount claims, a new Food and Grocery Code effective July 2026, and persistent political scrutiny of supermarket pricing create headline and potential financial risk (fines, code compliance costs, or structural remedies)

Wage underpayment costs could still grow: despite the ~A$710M H1 FY2026 provision, management has flagged further remediation, interest, superannuation and payroll tax exposure is possible as litigation and remediation processes continue, with risk of additional charges

New Zealand Food and BIG W turnarounds are not yet proven over a full cycle: NZ Food suffered a second-half earnings dip in FY2026 from store-operating-model disruption, and a prior A$1,492M FY2024 goodwill impairment underscores the segment's structural challenges; BIG W's return to profit is only one year old

Valuation reflects optimism already: post-results broker price-target upgrades (Bell Potter, Morgans) have been met with a more cautious broader sell-side consensus (closer to Hold, with some Sell ratings), suggesting the market sees limited further re-rating room unless the recovery proves durable
